# AD compromise is an edge path, not a single bug

## Claim

A user has a right over an object that leads to another right, then to a session on a high-value host.

## Test

Collect with BloodHound. Read the ACL edges. Pick the shortest path to the objective and prove one edge.

## Proof

A password reset, ticket or session that grants the next node, with the path in BloodHound.

## Failure modes

A roastable account with a strong password is not a finding until cracked. A path that needs DA to start is circular.

failure: A roastable account with a strong password is not a finding until cracked. A path that needs DA to start is circular.

# ESC1 is an enrollable SAN on a client-auth template

## Claim

A template lets a low-privilege principal enroll and supply a subject alternative name for another identity.

## Test

Read the template flags. Enroll with an arbitrary UPN. Use the certificate for PKINIT or Schannel.

A TGT or session as the target user from the crafted certificate.

## Failure modes

A template with approval or no client auth is not ESC1. Check the CA and the version.

# Indirect injection turns a document into an instruction

## Claim

A retrieved chunk contains instructions that the model follows, especially when a tool can send data out.

## Test

Plant an instruction in a document. Ask a normal question. Watch for a tool call with attacker arguments.

## Proof

A tool call or output that crosses the boundary without a user instruction.

## Failure modes

A prompt that says ignore previous instructions is not impact until the tool acts.

# RAG leaks when retrieval ignores the tenant

## Claim

The retriever ranks chunks across users and filters after generation, or not at all.

## Test

Create two users with distinct documents. Query as A and inspect the retrieved sources and the answer.

## Proof

A document from user B appears in A's answer or source list.

## Failure modes

A shared public doc is not a leak. A model hallucination is not retrieval.

# Cloud metadata is a credential endpoint

## Claim

A workload can reach the metadata service. The returned role may have more permission than the app needs.

## Test

Query the metadata endpoint. Get the role and temporary credentials. Call get-caller-identity. Test read-only permissions.

## Proof

A read-only API response that proves the role's effective access.

## Failure modes

A role name is not a permission. IMDSv2 blocks naive requests.

# x86_64 ROP needs the argument registers

## Claim

The first six arguments are rdi, rsi, rdx, rcx, r8, r9. A chain needs pop gadgets or a function that sets them.

## Test

Find pop rdi; ret. Put /bin/sh in a writable location. Call system or execve through a PLT or libc leak.

## Proof

A shell or a controlled call with the arguments visible in the debugger.

## Failure modes

A chain that assumes NX off fails on the target. libc offsets differ by build.

# UAF becomes control when the freed slot is reallocated

## Claim

A stale pointer is used after free. Reallocating the same size with controlled bytes replaces the object.

## Test

Free the object. Allocate the same size and fill it. Trigger the stale method. If it is a vtable, point it at a fake table.

## Proof

A controlled callback or write from the stale object.

## Failure modes

A UAF crash without reallocation is not control. Allocator behavior differs by version.

# Recall before searching

## Claim

Repeated research is waste. Check the knowledge index first, then refresh only a stale or low-confidence card.

## Test

Run recall with the target and class. If the decision is USE, answer from the card and test it. If REFRESH, verify one claim. If RESEARCH, collect.

## Proof

A card id and its proof, or a deliberate gap.

## Failure modes

A card can be stale. Check the date and the source before trusting it.

# A crash is a lead; the primitive is the finding

## Claim

A crash becomes a finding when you can name the controlled bytes, the fault address, the instruction pointer and the blocking mitigation.

## Test

Reproduce outside the fuzzer. Read registers and stack. Classify the fault. Minimize. Check mitigations.

## Proof

A controlled address or RIP, or a bounded leak, with a repeatable input.

## Failure modes

A null dereference is low. A crash under ASAN only can still be real but needs reachability.

# GhidRust is a paused Ghidra plugin, not Ghidrust

## Claim

DMaroo/GhidRust is a Ghidra extension for Rust binaries. oofz/Ghidrust is a separate Rust-native platform. Ghidra upstream Rust support is now better than the plugin.

## Test

Check the repo. Use GhidRust for its libstd FunctionID only when the Rust version matches. Use Ghidrust when you need a headless CLI/MCP.

## Proof

A function named by FunctionID, or a clean build from source.

## Failure modes

The C-to-Rust view is flaky. Do not present it as source.

## Claim

A slice is pointer plus length. A trait object is data plus vtable. Option uses a null niche. Async is a state machine.

## Test

# Cache poisoning is an unkeyed input that changes the response

## Claim

A header, cookie or query changes the response but not the cache key. A shared cache then serves it to another user.

## Test

Map the key. Change one unkeyed input. Poison with a unique value and request from a clean session.

## Proof

A clean request returns the attacker value, with cache headers showing a hit.

## Failure modes

A hit for your own cookie is not global. Vary and normalization can invalidate the result.

# Desync needs two HTTP parsers and an ambiguous length

## Claim

A front end and back end disagree about where a request ends, usually through Content-Length, Transfer-Encoding or HTTP/2 downgrade.

## Test

Send ambiguous requests. Try CL.TE, TE.CL, TE.TE, CRLF header injection and HTTP/2 pseudo-header tricks. Confirm with timing and a second client.

## Proof

A second clean client receives the wrong response, or a repeatable timing signal.

## Failure modes

One 400 does not prove desync. Shared proxies make results non-deterministic.

## Claim

The gateway checks the query but resolvers do not check the object, field or mutation. Introspection is a map, not a finding.

body:
# IDOR is a missing owner check, not a hidden id

## Claim

An object id from the request is used without comparing the object owner to the session user. Hiding the id in a UUID does not add a check.

## Test

Create two accounts at the same role. Capture an object id from A. Request it with B. Repeat for read, update, delete and export.

## Proof

B receives or changes A's object, with both sessions and the ids in the log.

## Failure modes

A public object, a 200 with an empty body, or an admin bypass is not the same bug. Check the data, not the status.

## Claim

The verifier trusts an algorithm, key or claim it should not. Decoding is not verification.

## Test

# OAuth redirect matching is prefix logic under pressure

## Claim

The authorization server compares redirect URIs with loose rules. Path traversal, a subdomain, an open redirect or a fragment can move the code.

## Test

Map every redirect URI and the matching rule. Test path, query, fragment, subdomain, case and open redirect on an allowed host. Reuse state and nonce.

## Proof

A code or token delivered to an attacker-controlled origin, then exchanged for a session.

## Failure modes

A login CSRF needs a victim action. A code for your own account is not account takeover.

body:
# A race is a check and a write without one lock

## Claim

The invariant is checked before a write, with no transaction or unique constraint. Parallel requests pass the same check.

## Test

Identify the invariant. Send parallel requests, ideally in one packet on HTTP/2. Compare successes with the intended limit.

## Proof

Two successes where one was allowed, with timestamps and request ids.

## Failure modes

A retry looks like a race. Server deduplication may hide it on a later request.

# SQL injection is a string-built query at a boundary

## Claim

User input reaches a query without a parameter binding. Escaping can fail when the charset, collation or parser changes.

## Test

Establish true and false baselines. Test quote, comment and parenthesis behavior. Move to time or OOB only when union and error are blocked.

## Proof

A bounded extraction of a value the tester should not see, with request and response.

## Failure modes

A WAF block looks like a false condition. Network jitter looks like a time delay. Do not dump the database.

# SSRF hides in URL parser disagreement

## Claim

One component validates a URL and another fetches it. Different parsers disagree about host, scheme, userinfo or path.

## Test

Use a listener to confirm the fetch. Test http:///host, backslashes, userinfo, encoded delimiters, IPv4-mapped IPv6, decimal IPs, redirects and DNS rebinding.

## Proof

A callback from the target, or a response body from an internal service.

## Failure modes

DNS-only SSRF is weak without exfiltration. A hit on your listener does not prove the response reaches the attacker.

proof: A callback from the target, or a response body from an internal service.
failure: DNS-only SSRF is weak without exfiltration. A hit on your listener does not prove the response reaches the attacker.

# Traversal is a join before canonicalization

## Claim

The app joins a user path to a root without resolving and checking the result. Encoded separators and absolute second arguments bypass naive filters.

## Test

Try ../, ..%2f, double encoding, absolute paths, null bytes and Windows separators. Compare the served file with the intended root.

Reflected filenames are not traversal. A 404 with the path in the body proves nothing.

# XSS survives when two parsers disagree

## Claim

A sanitizer, template engine or WAF reads the input with a different parser than the browser. The gap is the payload space.

## Test

Map the sanitizer and the sink. Try mXSS, namespace changes, comment tricks, attribute boundaries and encoding that normalizes late.

## Proof

Script execution in the target origin, with the exact input and browser.

## Failure modes

A payload that fires in an innerHTML test may not fire in the page. A CSP report without execution is not a finding.
